---
title: "Exercise: acceptor photobleaching"
---

## Goal

By the end of this exercise you should be able to:

- compute $E$ from the donor before and after acceptor photobleaching,
- correct it for **incomplete bleaching** and **donor bleaching**, and recognise **motion** and **photoconversion**,
- estimate the noise of a pixel-wise $E$ and explain why a region sum is better,
- explain why intensity methods measure the **apparent** efficiency $f \cdot E$, and what that means for distances,
- choose between sensitised emission, acceptor photobleaching and lifetimes for a given question,
- *(math)* derive the incomplete-bleaching correction, $E_\text{app} = fE$, and $\sigma_E$.

Do the pen-and-paper part first, then the demo.

## Background

| Idea | What it means |
|---|---|
| Dequenching | without acceptor the donor keeps all its excitations and gets brighter |
| Efficiency | $E = 1 - I_D^\text{pre}/I_D^\text{post}$ |
| Incomplete bleaching | fraction $b$ of the acceptor bleached: $E_\text{obs} = bE/(1 - (1 - b)E)$, corrected $E = E_\text{obs}/(b + (1 - b)E_\text{obs})$ |
| Donor bleaching | divide the post values by a control region's after/before ratio |
| Motion | align before dividing |
| Photoconversion | control: acceptor-only cells must not gain donor signal |
| Apparent efficiency | $E_\text{app} = fE$ ($f$: fraction of donors with an acceptor) |
| Noise of $1 - P/Q$ | $\sigma_E \approx (P/Q)\sqrt{1/P + 1/Q}$ (Poisson) |

## By hand

**B1.** The donor in the bleach region averages 600 photons per pixel before and 800 after. Compute $E$.

**B2.** The acceptor image shows 20 % of the acceptor left after bleaching ($b = 0.8$).
(a) Is the $E$ of B1 too high or too low?
(b) Correct it.
(c) Check your answer: with the corrected $E$ and $b = 0.8$, what would the observed $E$ be?

**B3.** A non-bleached part of the same cell went from 500 to 475 photons (−5 %).
(a) Correct the $E$ of B1 for donor bleaching.
(b) Apply both corrections (donor bleaching, then incomplete bleaching with $b = 0.8$).

**B4.** **Pixel noise.** Assume Poisson counts.
(a) $\sigma_E$ for a pixel with 600 before and 800 after.
(b) The same for 60 and 80 photons (ten times dimmer).
(c) A region of 100 pixels at 60/80: what is $\sigma_E$ of the region if you sum first?

**B5.** **Apparent efficiency.** A population gives $E_\text{app} = 0.2$, $R_0 = 5$ nm.
(a) Interpretation 1: all donors paired. What is the distance?
(b) Interpretation 2: half the donors paired. What is $E$ of a pair, and the distance?
(c) What measurement would decide?

**B6.** **Which method?** For each question choose sensitised emission (SE), acceptor photobleaching (AP) or donor lifetime (FLIM) and justify in one line:
(a) Does a kinase sensor change FRET within seconds after adding a drug, in living cells?
(b) Do two proteins interact at all in fixed cells; you have no single-labelled controls on this microscope?
(c) Is the change in $E_\text{app}$ caused by more binding or by a shorter distance?

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Solutions"}
**B1.** $E = 1 - 600/800 = 0.25$.

**B2.** (a) Too low: 20 % of the donors are still quenched after bleaching, so the donor did not rise fully. (b) $E = 0.25/(0.8 + 0.2\cdot0.25) = 0.25/0.85 = 0.294$. (c) $0.8\cdot0.294/(1 - 0.2\cdot0.294) = 0.235/0.941 = 0.25$.

**B3.** (a) The donor lost 5 % by itself, so the true post value is $800/0.95 = 842$: $E = 1 - 600/842 = 0.2875$ (0.287). (b) $0.2875/(0.8 + 0.2\cdot0.2875) = 0.2875/0.8575 = 0.335$. Both corrections raise $E$; together they move it from 0.25 to 0.34.

**B4.** (a) $0.75\sqrt{1/600 + 1/800} = 0.75\cdot0.0540 = 0.0405$. (b) $0.75\sqrt{1/60 + 1/80} = 0.128$. (c) Summing 100 pixels gives $P = 6000$, $Q = 8000$: $\sigma_E = 0.75\sqrt{1/6000 + 1/8000} = 0.0128$, ten times smaller than one pixel.

**B5.** (a) $r = 5\,(1/0.2 - 1)^{1/6} = 5\cdot4^{1/6} = 6.30$ nm ($1.26R_0$). (b) $E = 0.2/0.5 = 0.4$, $r = 5\,(1.5)^{1/6} = 5.35$ nm ($1.07R_0$). (c) The donor's lifetime decay: interpretation 1 has one shortened lifetime ($0.8\,\tau_D$), interpretation 2 has two components, $\tau_D$ and $0.6\,\tau_D$, in equal amounts.

**B6.** (a) SE (or FLIM): it can be repeated over time in living cells; AP destroys the acceptor and takes time. (b) AP: it needs no bleed-through coefficients and works well in fixed cells (no diffusion back into the region). (c) FLIM: lifetimes separate $f$ and $E$; intensity methods only give their product.
:::

### Math questions

**B7.** *(math)* All donors paired, each acceptor bleached independently with probability $b$. (a) Show that the donor intensity after bleaching is proportional to $1 - (1 - b)E$ and that $E_\text{obs} = bE/(1 - (1 - b)E)$. (b) Solve for $E$. (c) Show that $E_\text{obs} < E$ for $0 < b < 1$ and $0 < E < 1$.

**B8.** *(math)* A fraction $f$ of the donors is paired at efficiency $E$, the rest are unpaired. (a) Show that complete acceptor bleaching gives $1 - I^\text{pre}/I^\text{post} = fE$. (b) Show that the sensitised-emission estimate $F_c/(F_c + G I_{DD})$ of unit 2 gives the same $fE$.

**B9.** *(math)* (a) Derive $\sigma_E \approx (P/Q)\sqrt{1/P + 1/Q}$ for $E = 1 - P/Q$ with independent Poisson $P$, $Q$. (b) Show that summing $m$ pixels before dividing reduces $\sigma_E$ by $\sqrt m$.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Solutions (math)"}
**B7.** (a) Before: every donor is quenched, intensity $\propto 1 - E$. After: a fraction $b$ has lost its acceptor (intensity 1), the rest are still quenched ($1 - E$): $b + (1 - b)(1 - E) = 1 - (1 - b)E$. $E_\text{obs} = 1 - (1 - E)/(1 - (1 - b)E) = (1 - (1 - b)E - 1 + E)/(1 - (1 - b)E) = bE/(1 - (1 - b)E)$. (b) $E_\text{obs} - (1 - b)EE_\text{obs} = bE$, so $E = E_\text{obs}/(b + (1 - b)E_\text{obs})$. (c) $E_\text{obs}/E = b/(1 - (1 - b)E)$; the denominator is larger than $b$ exactly when $1 - b > (1 - b)E$, i.e. $E < 1$: so $E_\text{obs} < E$.

**B8.** (a) Before: $(1 - f)\cdot1 + f(1 - E) = 1 - fE$. After: all donors unquenched, 1. So $1 - (1 - fE)/1 = fE$. (b) In unit 2's model, $I_{DD} \propto c_{DD}N_D(1 - fE)$ and $F_c = G c_{DD}N_D fE$: $F_c/(F_c + G I_{DD}) = fE/(fE + 1 - fE) = fE$.

**B9.** (a) $\partial E/\partial P = -1/Q$, $\partial E/\partial Q = P/Q^2$; independent, so $\sigma_E^2 \approx \sigma_P^2/Q^2 + P^2\sigma_Q^2/Q^4 = P/Q^2 + P^2/Q^3 = (P/Q)^2(1/P + 1/Q)$. (b) Summing $m$ pixels replaces $P, Q$ by $mP, mQ$: the ratio $P/Q$ is unchanged, $1/(mP) + 1/(mQ) = (1/P + 1/Q)/m$, so $\sigma_E$ shrinks by $\sqrt m$.
:::

## Explore: bleach the acceptor {#explore}

Two FRET cells (true $E$ and paired fraction $f$ from the sliders) and an acceptor-only control cell (bottom left in the acceptor image), seeded with Poisson noise. The yellow box is the bleach region (drag on "donor before" to draw another); the acceptor-only cell is bleached as a whole. Each pulse bleaches 30 % of the acceptor left in the region. Tiles: donor before, donor after, acceptor after, $E$ map ($1 - \text{pre}/\text{post}$ per pixel, white = 0, red positive, blue negative). Plot: expected donor and acceptor in the region and donor outside it, per pulse. Readouts: region $E$ as a ratio of sums, the mean of the pixel values, the truth, the acceptor left, the control's after/before ratio, the acceptor-only cell's donor channel.

```{=html}
<link rel="stylesheet" href="../demos/dist/demo.css">
<div data-demo="apbleach" data-preset="ideal"></div>
<script src="../demos/dist/apbleach.js"></script>
```

**E1.** Preset **ideal**. Read the region $E$ (ratio of sums), the mean of the pixel $E$ values and the acceptor left. What does the $E$ map show outside the box? Set the pulses to 0: what is $E$ now, and why is it not exactly 0?

**E2.** Preset **stop early: incomplete bleaching** (4 pulses). Read $E$ and the acceptor left. Predict the corrected value with the formula, then tick **correct incomplete bleaching** and compare.

**E3.** Preset **donor bleaching fakes less FRET** (1.5 % per pulse). Read $E$ and the control's after/before ratio. Predict the size of the error from the ratio, then tick **correct donor bleaching**. What does the $E$ map look like outside the box before the correction?

**E4.** Preset **the cell moved: edges** (3 px drift). Describe the $E$ map. Why does the "acceptor left" readout go wrong too? Tick **align after to before**: what shift is found, and what $E$?

**E5.** Preset **few photons: noisy map, region fine** (40 photons). Read the region $E$, the mean of the pixel $E$ values and estimate the pixel spread from the map. Then smooth with σ = 2. Which number is closer to the truth, and why are the two different?

**E6.** Preset **half the donors paired** ($f = 0.5$, $E = 0.3$). Read $E$. Then set $f = 1$ and $E = 0.15$. Can you tell the two situations apart from anything in the demo?

**E7.** Preset **photoconversion: the control lights up**. Read the acceptor-only cell's donor channel before and after and the region $E$. What would you conclude without the acceptor-only control?

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Solutions"}
**E1.** Region $E$ = 0.297, mean of pixel $E$ = 0.295 (true 0.30); 0.5 % acceptor left. Outside the box the map is white with noise (about 0): the acceptor is intact there. With 0 pulses, $E$ = −0.002 (pixel mean −0.006): before and after are two independent noisy images of the same donor, so the ratio fluctuates around 1.

**E2.** $E$ = 0.244 with 24.1 % acceptor left ($b = 0.759$). Formula: $0.244/(0.759 + 0.241\cdot0.244) = 0.298$; the demo gives 0.298 with the correction.

**E3.** $E$ = 0.117, control ratio 0.796: the donor lost 20 % by itself, which eats most of the 43 % rise from dequenching ($1/0.7 = 1.43$; $1.43 \cdot 0.80 = 1.14$, so $E \approx 1 - 1/1.14 = 0.12$). Correcting: post divided by 0.796 gives $E$ = 0.298. Before the correction the map outside the box is blue (negative $E$): the donor got dimmer there.

**E4.** Red edges on one side of each cell and blue on the other: the after image is displaced. The acceptor sum in the box is computed on the displaced image, so part of the unbleached acceptor slides into the box: 20.8 % "left" instead of 0.5 %, and $E$ = 0.275 (pixel mean 0.255, spread 0.15). Alignment finds the shift (−3, −2) and gives $E$ = 0.297 again.

**E5.** Region $E$ = 0.292, pixel mean 0.270, pixel spread about 0.20 (the map is speckle). With σ = 2 the spread drops to about 0.05 and the map is readable, but the pixel mean stays low (0.267). The ratio of sums divides two large, precise numbers; the mean of pixel ratios averages ratios of small noisy numbers, which are biased (unit 4). Smoothing reduces the spread, not this bias of $1 - P/Q$ in dim pixels.

**E6.** $f = 0.5$, $E = 0.3$: region $E$ = 0.147 ($fE = 0.15$). With $f = 1$, $E = 0.15$ the region $E$ is also about 0.15. The demo shows only intensities; nothing distinguishes the two. Only the donor's lifetime decay (two components or one) would.

**E7.** The acceptor-only cell's donor channel goes from 0 to 70 per pixel, and the region $E$ rises to 0.388 (true 0.30): photoconverted acceptors add donor-coloured light, which looks like dequenching. Without the control you would report too much FRET.
:::

## Where this leads

The efficiency in every intensity method is $f \cdot E$; lifetimes separate them, which is a main reason for **FLIM** (FLIM day): $E = 1 - \tau_{DA}/\tau_D$ from the rate picture of the first unit. The next unit turns to the simplest and most used FRET measurement, the **ratio** of two channels of a single-chain biosensor, and to the statistics of ratios that already appeared here.
